thread.title: Stock Market Trims Trump China Gains; Cat Upgraded| Investor's Business Daily

author: ALAN R. ELLIOTT
title: Stock Market Trims Trump China Gains; Cat Upgraded| Investor's Business Daily

organizations.name: stock market trims trump china gains

text:
The Dow Jones industrial average opened more than 400-points higher but the stock market quickly trimmed early gains Monday receiving a boost from weekend trade negotiations in Argentina.
X China-based stocks rallied hard. Among the leaders was Weibo ( WB ), which had just overtaken an important technical marker on Friday. Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Nvidia ( NVDA ) and ST Microelectronics ( STM ) led surging chipmakers.
Apple ( AAPL ) muscled up more than 3% and Amazon.com ( AMZN ) scrambled to the head of the hard-charging FANG stocks . Biomed Tesaro ( TSRO ) bolted higher on news it would be acquired by GlaxoSmithKline ( GSK ). Shares of cannabis-related New Age Beverage ( NBEV ) spiked after the company announced an $85 million acquisition.
The Dow Jones industrial average narrowed its opening gain to 1.4%. The S&P 500 advanced 1.1%. Dow Jones stock Boeing ( BA ) spiked 6%, and Caterpillar ( CAT ) swept more than 4% higher. Wynn Resorts ( WYNN ) — a leading stakeholder in China's Macau gaming capital — and AMD traded at the top of the S&P 500.
The Nasdaq Composite pared its opening rally to 1.3% — as it struggled to hold its 50-day moving average. Wynn Resorts, biomed Incyte ( INCY ) and Nvidia led its early advance.

That positions investors to make new purchases early Monday. Stocks set to break out past buy points include blue chips Microsoft ( MSFT ), Visa ( V ), Boeing and Mastercard ( MA ), among others.
The country also begins the week in mourning for former President George H.W. Bush, who died late Friday. Stock and bond markets will remain closed on Wednesday in observance of an official day of mourning announced by the White House .
Trump China Trade Policy A meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping in Argentina ended with the U.S. agreeing to delay for 90 days a planned increase on tariffs imposed on China-made imports valued at $200 billion per year. China reportedly agreed to increase its purchases of agricultural, industrial and energy goods.
Early Monday, Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin said in a CNBC interview that China had made commitments, giving the Argentina agreement some potential authority.
The Trump administration launched its economic war in January, imposing tariffs of 15% to 50% on a fairly tight range of China-made goods including washing machines and solar energy panels. In March, the administration added a round of tariffs against steel and aluminum imports from all countries, except Canada and Mexico, in a move that specifically targeted China.
The larger-scale tariffs began in July, with duties of 25% on $50 billion in China-made goods initiated July 6; Beijing immediately responded, imposing duties on U.S. imports valued at $34 billion per year. On Aug. 23, the White House added 25% tariffs on another round of goods, valued at $16 billion. China again responded in kind.
On Sept. 24, the U.S. added new tariffs of 10% on China-made imports valued at $200 billion annually. China responded with tariffs on U.S. goods worth $60 billion. The 10% U.S. tariffs were set to increase to 25% on Jan. 1.
This weekend's agreement gives the two countries until April 1 to negotiate trade terms on issues the White House says will include forced technology transfer and intellectual property theft. If no agreement is achieved, the U.S. tariffs on $200 billion in China-based goods would increase from 10% to 25%.
Hong Kong Exits Bear Market; Europe Rallies Global markets rallied on the trade news. In China, the Shanghai Composite surged 2.7%, the tech-heavy Shenzhen Composite bolted 3.3% higher, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index soared 2.6%. The Hang Seng's advance lifted the benchmark to within 19% of its February high, lifting it out of bear market territory for the first time since the beginning of October.
In Japan, Tokyo's Nikkei 225 gained 1%, retaking its 50-day moving average in its seventh straight gain. Stocks with high exposure to China's markets powered the gain.
That was also the case in Europe, although stocks there were trading well off their earlier highs in afternoon action. Frankfurt's DAX held a 2.1% gain, with London's FTSE 100 up 1.6% and the CAC-40 in Paris showing a 0.9% gain.
Among other global markets, Taiwan's TaiEx gained 2.5% and Greece's Athex leapt 4.1%, while India's leading benchmarks gained only a fraction.
Oil Prices Rally On Trade, OPEC/Russia Oil prices ran up more than 4%, sending West Texas Intermediate above $53 a barrel and Brent crude to near $62. A trade war truce eases concerns of deeper tariffs cutting into oil, auto prices and oil demand in China and the U.S. In addition, a Saturday meeting in Argentina yielded an agreement between Russia and Saudi Arabia to continue their partnership in balancing global oil production with demand. Russia is scheduled to meet with the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries in Vienna on Thursday.
Oil prices ended Friday 34% below an early October slide, following a seven-week slide that marked oil's longest (though not deepest) decline in a half century.
Boeing, Amazon, Tesla, Nike Climb; Caterpillar Upgraded Boeing rumbled 6.1% higher, positioning it just below a 373.80 buy point. Caterpillar powered up 4% after being upgrded to buy, from neutral, by Bank of America. The note raised the stock's price target to 163, from 140. Visa and Mastercard each rose around 2%, placing them very close to their respective buy points .
Nike ( NKE ) clocked a 4% gain after JPMorgan hoisted its price target to 85, from 81. The move put shares back above their 10-week moving average, starting up the right side of a possible base pattern.
Amazon hammered 4.3% higher, launching the stock back above its converged 10- and 40-week moving averages.
Automaker stocks jumped on trade relief. Tesla swung up 3.8% in premarket trade. That put shares within 2% of a 366.75 buy point in a three-month cup-with-handle base. Tesla stock has been stalled below resistance near 370 for 17 months.
General Motors ( GM ) jumped 2.9%, Ford ( F ) punched up 4.6% and Fiat Chrysler ( FCAU ) seized a 2.8% gain.
China's Autohome ( ATHM ) vaulted to 6.6% to lead the IBD 50 list. The stock is working to build the right side of a possible five-month base pattern.
Adobe ( ADBE ) alimbed 1.6% at the open. The stock is trading below a potential 277.71 buy point in a possible base pattern.
Trade Desk ( TTD ) rolled up a 1.3% gain, which moved it closer to a 161.60 buy point.
Ciena Corp. ( CIEN ) edged up 0.9% in early trade.. The IBD Leaderboard stock ended Friday back in a buy range above a 32.43 buy point after clearing a flat base in early November.
M&A: Glaxo/Tesaro, New Age Beverage/Morinda Cancer treatment biotech Tesaro spiraled 59% higher, after GlaxoSmithKline announced it would acquire the company for $4.16 billion in cash. The $75 per share offer was 62% above Tesaro's closing price on Friday. Glaxo shares fell 6.9% in premarket trade.
New Age Beverage, maker of cannabidoil-based, or CBD-based drinks, spiked 6% after the company said it would pay $85 million to acquire Utah-based Morinda. New Age beverage shares had fallen to less than 5. Among other cannabis-related names, Canopy Growth ( CGC ) jumped 1.2%, Aurora Cannabis ( ACB ) slipped 0.5% and Cronos Group ( CRON ) fell almost 2%.
Chicago's Tribune Media ( TRCO ) shot nearly 10% higher Monday, after Nexstar Media Group ( NXST ) agreed to buy the television and radio operator in a deal valued near $6.4 billion. The deal, which would make Nexstar the largest U.S. television operator, comes four months after Sinclair Broadcast Group ( SBGI ) scuttled its buyout attempt. Nexstar shares rose 2.8% at the open.
